summary: Ridge lookout in Lemhi/Idaho County, ID: two-story log-frame cab dated 1934; gone per two lookout pages; newspaper items show staff in 1951 and 1954.

facts.status_note: Both lookout pages list it as Gone; neither gives a date or cause

access.note: No source describes the ridge today or who controls it

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as a hike-in

facts.agency: Bitterroot National Forest per two sources; Salmon National Forest per one

events.note: Two-story log-frame cab on a ridge a quarter mile south of the summit, per the lookout lists
High-frequency radios reported at the Stoddard and West Horse lookouts (Recorder-Herald item, July 13, 1950)
Couple from East Lansing, Michigan, came to man the post (July 12, 1951 item)
Mr. and Mrs. Bill Powell kept inside the lookout for two days by a bull moose (September 2, 1954 item)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts place the site in the Bitterroot National Forest; Forest Lookouts places it in the Salmon National Forest. The story reports both and does not choose.
Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history; the Forest Lookouts page quotes 1950 to 1954 newspaper items about the lookout. Both are reported as stated.

notes_for_editor: Gone status is consistent across the two lookout pages but no date or cause is given. Forest attribution conflicts (Bitterroot in two sources, Salmon in one); the story reports the conflict. Staffing rests on newspaper items quoted by one page (Forest Lookouts); Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no staffing history. The 1934 date is the cab date from the lists. No photos were found with usable URLs. One WebSearch used; it added no page with new dated facts.
